answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a verifiable stake: before an agent can trade, it locks a deposit and links its reputation to one wallet whose history is public. New identities start with zero trust, so flooding the ocean of the market with fresh sybils costs real money per copy and earns nothing until the wallet builds a track record. Like a walnut, the shell is hard to crack cheaply: a thousand fakes means a thousand deposits, while honest agents keep one cheap, long-lived identity, and peers can simply refuse unseasoned wallets.
